title: Ephemeral scanner profiles & remediation-bundle spec
content:
Purpose

This doc proposes a lightweight architecture for ephemeral scanner identities (RBAC v2-aware), and a signed remediation-bundle format ("proof-of-remediation") that can be emitted after a successful patch/mitigation run. The goal is to: 1) minimize blast radius of scanner credentials, 2) create machine-verifiable remediation evidence that maps to our audit schema and SIEM exports, and 3) streamline automated handoffs into the incident/patch tracking pipeline.

Problem statement / motivation
- Current scanner runs use long-lived service credentials (scoped to a team or environment) which increases risk if a scanner token is leaked or over-privileged.
- Remediation state is dispersed: ticket comments, S3 blobs, and ad-hoc logs. Hard to cryptographically prove "what changed" and when.
- SIEM exports currently ingest scanner findings but struggle to tie subsequent patch events back to the original scan in a tamper-evident way.

Proposal overview
- Ephemeral scanner profiles: short-lived, constrained RBAC v2 tokens minted by the security control plane per-scan. Tokens are scoped to a single scan run and model (scanner type, ruleset id, target scope).
- Remediation-bundle: a small JSONL bundle produced by remediation automation that includes: scan_id, list of patched items (package@version or image digest), patch commands executed, artifact URIs (signed), timestamp, operator identity, and a KMS-backed signature.
- Audit/SIEM mapping: standardize an "evidence" event_type in the audit log schema to reference remediation-bundles. SIEM mappings will index bundle attributes for search/fusion with original findings.

Requirements (non-exhaustive)
- Scanner token lifespan: default 30 minutes, configurable up to 4 hours for long-running infra scans. Tokens must be single-run and non-renewable.
- Minimal privileges: tokens should only allow list/scan/read on target asset inventory and upload of bundle to the evidence bucket/prefix with ACL write-signed-metadata permission.
- Bundle signature: use KMS asymmetric keys (customer-managed for Private customers) to sign the remediation-bundle manifest. Signature plus manifest stored as object metadata and exported into the audit log.
- Traceability: every remediation action must reference the scanner scan_id and ticket id (Jira/Linear). The remediation-bundle must include a field: original_findings_refs: [finding_id...].

Proposed remediation-bundle schema (flat fields, example lines below)
Note: this is a text spec for the bundle; final wire format is JSONL (one object per patched item) plus a signed manifest.
- bundle_id: rbdl-<YYYYMMDD>-<random6>
- scan_id: scanner:trivy:20251110:abcd1234
- operator: maya.thompson@redwood.ai (or service:patcher@redwood.ai)
- ticket_id: SEC-7123
- patched_items: ["pkg:deb/debian/curl@7.68.0-1ubuntu2.10","docker:sha256:abcd..."]
- commands_executed: ["apt-get install --only-upgrade curl=7.68.0-1ubuntu2.11","kubectl set image deployment/foo foo=registry/release:1.2.3"]
- artifact_uris: ["s3://evidence-bucket/ephemeral/2025-11-10/rbdl-abcd1234/manifest.json","s3://evidence-bucket/ephemeral/.../patch.log"]
- manifest_signature: <base64sig>
- signer_key_id: projects/redwood/locations/global/keyRings/sec/cryptoKeys/rbdl-key/cryptoKeyVersions/1
- completed_at: 2025-11-10T18:42:09Z
- remediation_status: fixed | mitigated | false_positive

Example bundle line (single patched item JSONL)
{ "bundle_id": "rbdl-20251110-6f3a2b", "scan_id": "trivy-20251110-abcd1234", "finding_ref": "trivy:pkg:deb/curl:HIGH:CVSS3.1:2025-11-10", "patched_to": "curl@7.68.0-1ubuntu2.11", "patch_command": "apt-get install --only-upgrade curl=7.68.0-1ubuntu2.11", "artifact_uri": "s3://evidence-bucket/.../curl-patch.log" }

RBAC v2 integration notes
- New role: roles/ephemeralScannerRunner (minimal verbs: scan:listTargets, scan:run, evidence:uploadTemp).
- Token minting flow: security-control-plane creates token after verifying requester identity + approval policy (e.g., only CI runners + on-call scanner service can request). Token metadata includes scan_id and ruleset_id.
- Token revocation: tokens recorded in short-lived cache; revocation can be immediate if suspicious activity detected. Logs must contain token_id and token_issuer.
- Edge case: cross-account/private deployments: for Private customers, token minting is delegated; evidence artifacts must be signed with customer KMS.

Audit log schema additions (high level)
Goal: allow SIEM to link scan findings -> remediation-bundle -> ticket -> deployment change using a small set of indexed fields.
Add/standardize these audit fields:
- event_type: vuln.scan.run | vuln.finding.reported | vuln.remediation.bundle.upload | vuln.remediation.action
- entity_id: e.g., instance id, image digest, package coordinate
- scan_id: unique id from scanner run
- finding_id: scanner-specific finding id
- bundle_id: remediation bundle id (if available)
- signer_key_id: KMS key version used to sign bundle
- evidence_uri: s3://... or gs://...
- outcome: success | failure | partial
- operator: principal who executed action
- correlation_keys: [ticket_id, deploy_id]

Sample audit event (vuln.remediation.bundle.upload)
- timestamp: 2025-11-10T18:42:10Z
- event_type: vuln.remediation.bundle.upload
- bundle_id: rbdl-20251110-6f3a2b
- scan_id: trivy-20251110-abcd1234
- operator: service:patcher@redwood.ai
- evidence_uri: s3://evidence-bucket/ephemeral/2025-11-10/rbdl-6f3a2b/manifest.json
- manifest_signature: <base64>
- signer_key_id: projects/redwood/.../rbdl-key/v1

SIEM export mapping notes (for SIEM team)
- Index bundle_id, scan_id, finding_id, signer_key_id, outcome, and ticket_id as top-level fields.
- Create a correlation view that connects vuln.finding.reported -> vuln.remediation.bundle.upload -> deploy.change events. Use a 7-day window by default, configurable per team.
- For high-severity findings (critical), create an automated correlation alert when a related remediation-bundle is not uploaded within 24 hours of the first confirmed finding.

Remediation / patch SLA matrix (recommended)
- Critical (CVSS >= 9, or exploitable RCE in prod): 24 hours detection->mitigation window; full patch within 72 hours or documented compensating control.
- High: 72 hours detection->mitigation; full patch within 10 days.
- Medium: 14 days
- Low: triage within 30 days

Escalation flow (example)
1) Scanner run uploads findings -> creates SEC ticket (auto) with scan_id.
2) If no remediation-bundle uploaded within SLA window, SIEM fires an alert to sec-oncall channel and opens escalation ticket (SEC-ESCL-<id>).
3) After 48 hours past SLA for Critical, page infra-team on-call and create cross-team war room.

Dependency review notes (scanning libraries & transitive deps)
- Use SBOM (CycloneDX) as part of scan input; remediation-bundle must include sbom_ref if used.
- For transitive dependency upgrades that require package rebuild, include a "rebuild_plan" field in the bundle describing CI jobs triggered and expected completion.

Operational Playbook (runbook excerpts)
- Pre-scan: request token via control-plane API: POST /v1/ephemeral-token {"scope":"image:registry/foo/*","ruleset":"nvd-2025-11"} -> returns token, token_id, expires_at.
- Scan: run scanner with token, collect findings, attach scan_id metadata to every finding.
- Patch: invoke remediation automation (service:patcher) with ticket_id + scan_id -> runs patch steps -> produces remediation-bundle -> signs with KMS -> uploads to evidence S3.
- Audit: upload event with event_type=vuln.remediation.bundle.upload to audit stream (prod-audit topic). Ensure SIEM is subscribed to that topic and mapping is applied.

Open questions / TODOs
- How long should we retain ephemeral evidence objects in the "ephemeral" prefix vs. move to a long-term archive? Propose 90 days in ephemeral, then immutable archive for compliance (7 years) — need legal signoff.
- Key rotation / signer_key_id lifecycle and how to re-verify old bundles after key rotation. Need a canonical KMS key registry in Confluence.
- Decide whether the bundle manifest itself is also submitted to Confluence ticket as an attachment or only to S3 (tradeoff: easier for auditors vs noisy ticket history).
- Evaluate scanner SDK support for embedding scan_id in every finding for Trivy, Grype, Snyk, and our in-house agent.

Notes to self / rough action items
- [ ] Draft control-plane API spec for ephemeral token minting (SEC-EPHEM-TOKENS).
- [ ] Prototype bundle signer using google-kms asymmetric keys (or vendor KMS abstraction).
- [ ] Add SIEM mapping PR to security-observability repo (SEC-SIEM-MAPPING-PR).
- [ ] Run 2-week pilot with infra team on non-prod image registry.

Appendix: example curl flows
1) mint token
curl -X POST https://control-plane.internal/v1/ephemeral-token \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN" \
  -d '{"scope":"image:registry/nonprod/*","ruleset":"nvd-2025-11","ttl_seconds":1800}'

2) upload signed bundle (after signing locally using KMS signer SDK)
curl -X PUT "https://s3.amazonaws.com/evidence-bucket/ephemeral/2025-11-10/rbdl-6f3a2b/manifest.json" \
  -H "x-amz-meta-signature: <base64sig>" --upload-file manifest.json

3) publish audit event (internal producer)
producer.publish(topic="prod-audit", payload={"event_type":"vuln.remediation.bundle.upload","bundle_id":"rbdl-20251110-6f3a2b","evidence_uri":"s3://.../manifest.json","signer_key_id":"projects/redwood/.../rbdl-key/v1"})

Endnotes
- This is intentionally a first-pass. The emphasis is on minimizing token blast radius, making remediation auditable and verifiable, and giving SIEM a compact mapping to connect scans and patches.
- Feedback requested: security-observability, infra, devtools, legal (retention), and product (impact on rollout cadence).

Last updated by: Maya Thompson (maya.thompson@redwood.ai) on 2025-11-20
